10 Things You Probably Did Not Know About Eraser Technology

In Britain, erasers themselves are still often called "rubbers." (Which may lead to some confusion, maybe.)

Nope. Rubbers just mean erasers in british english, not condoms (those are just called condoms). An eraser, if it means anything, is the name for those wipers you get for whiteboards.

  1. Pencils with built-in erasers on the tops are a largely American phenomenon. Most pencils sold in Europe are eraser-less. Read into that cultural difference what you will.

While you certainly can get eraserless pencils, I'm not so sure about the "most" part.

  1. The little erasers on pencil ends are known as "plugs." Yep. And those small bands of metal that contain the plugs are called "ferrules."

That's also the name for the rubber knobs on the end of walking sticks and some furniture legs.

  1. Many of today's most high-tech erasers are made of vinyl. While the pink erasers you find on pencils are made of synthetic rubber, an increasing number of erasers are made of vinyl. Vinyl's durability and flexibility give erasers made of it "minimal crumbling," and offer, overall, "first-class erasing performance." Plus, obviously, the sound quality is richer with vinyl.

If you ever feel the need for a custom erasing experience, try a putty rubber. They're mostly for erasing very soft pencil, but you can work it into whatever size and shape you need to get the perfect mark.
